proposed.text: An architectural firm assigned economic copyright in a commercial-complex design to the developer by written agreement. What rights may still remain with the architect-author under RA 8293?

options.text: The architect-author may still assert non-assignable moral rights such as attribution and integrity, but not the assigned economic licensing rights
The architect-author keeps all economic copyright despite the written assignment
The architect-author may enforce economic copyright against the developer whenever the developer licenses the design
The architect-author retains moral rights only if the assignment agreement expressly reserved them

rationale.c: This treats assigned economic rights as if they remained with the assignor.
rationale.d: Moral rights are statutory; they are not dependent on an express reservation in the assignment.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180 allows economic copyright assignment in whole or in part. Sections 193 and 198 keep moral rights personal to the author and state that they are not assignable or subject to license. Section 195 allows waiver only within statutory limits. After assignment, the architect-author may still have moral-rights claims, but the assigned economic licensing rights belong to the assignee within the assignment scope.
rationale.takeaway: Assignment transfers economic rights within its scope; moral rights remain personal and non-assignable.

proposed.explanation: Rewrote the scenario to avoid saying moral rights enforce economic licensing after assignment.
